snp4.10:1.2:
is one said to be
at peace?
snp4.10:1.3:
Gotama, tell me about
—when asked about—
snp4.10:2.1:
The Buddha:
“Free from craving
before the break-up
[of the body],
independent
of before
snp4.10:3.4:
he is a sage,
his speech
under control.
snp4.10:4.1:
Free from attachment
with regard to the future,
snp4.10:4.3:
he sees seclusion
in the midst of sensory contacts.
snp4.10:4.4:
He can’t be led
in terms of views.
snp4.10:5.4:
he doesn’t engage in
divisive speech.
snp4.10:7.3:
Unobstructed by craving,
he doesn’t through craving
snp4.10:8.3:
equal,
superior,
inferior,
in the world.
snp4.10:8.4:
No swellings of pride
are his.
snp4.10:9.3: in whom no craving is found
snp4.10:10.1:
He is said
to be at peace,
snp4.10:10.3:
with nothing at all
to tie him down:
snp4.10:11.3:
In him you can’t pin down
what’s embraced
or rejected.
snp4.10:12.2:
for that which people run-of-the-mill
or brahmans & contemplatives
snp4.10:12.4:
which is why
he is unperturbed
with regard to their words.
snp4.10:13.2:
the sage
doesn’t speak of himself
snp4.10:13.3:
as among those who are higher,
equal,
or lower.
snp4.10:13.4:
He,
theory-free,
goes to no theory.
snp4.10:14.1:
For whom
nothing in the world
is his own,
snp4.10:14.2:
who doesn’t grieve
over what is not,
snp4.10:14.3:
who doesn’t enter into
doctrines
phenomena:
snp4.10:14.4:
He is said
to be
at peace.”
